alt: Before you automate anything, ask these five questions.
Automate the right tasks: Some save hours - Same steps, every time.; Some add mess - Unclear steps just run faster.; Some need you - Judgment calls stay human.
The five questions: How often does it happen?; Is it done the same way?; How much time does it cost?; What if it goes wrong?; Who checks the result?
Often, and the same way every time?. Frequent, repeatable tasks are the best candidates. If the steps change each time, write them down before you automate.
Hypothetical figures. Example: order confirmations: How often Every day; Same steps? Yes; Time cost Adds up; Risk if wrong Low; Human check Quick spot check; Verdict Good candidate
Keep a human on exceptions. Fine to automate: Routine confirmations; Copying the same data. Keep a human: Refund disputes; Upset customers
Score one task: Does it repeat often?; Are the steps the same?; Does it cost real time?; Is a mistake easy to catch?

caption:
Before you automate anything, ask these five questions. 🤖

Automation is great when the work repeats and the steps are clear. It is not great when it just makes a messy process run faster.

Swipe for a quick check:
✅ How often does it happen?
✅ Is it done the same way each time?
✅ How much time does it cost?
✅ What happens if it goes wrong?
✅ Who checks the result?

Score one task from your week and see if it passes.

💾 Save this post for the next time you're tempted to automate something.
